extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (U.S. students, recent graduates, artists, and non‑U.S. applicants seeking Fulbright awards to the U.S.)
extracted.subtask_short: applying to fulbright us student awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility requirements for applying to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program, including the main award categories (Study/Research, English Teaching Assistant, and special programs) and program‑specific eligibility rules. Covers who should apply through a U.S. institution, who should apply via foreign Fulbright Commissions/U.S. Embassies, and special fellowships (Fogarty, National Geographic).

rubrics_metrics.name: National competition deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The national deadline is Tuesday October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the national deadline; check the current competition year page for the exact deadline and local/institutional deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Current U.S. Student
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If currently enrolled at a U.S. college or university, you must apply through that institution even if you are not currently a resident there. Find and work with the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — U.S. Citizen but not a Student
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. citizens who will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date and do not have a Ph.D. are eligible to apply as non‑enrolled applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying. Candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. See the Getting Started page for details on eligibility and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Artists / Creative & Performing Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arts candidates should have relatively limited professional experience (typically 7 years or less); artists with more experience should consider the Fulbright Scholar Program. Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / route — U.S. Professors and Administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. professors or administrators interested in a Fulbright Scholar Award must apply through fulbrightscholars.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page is for the U.S. Student Program; professors/administrators should use the Fulbright Scholar application channel. To support student applicants, faculty should connect with their institution’s Fulbright Program Adviser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / route — Non‑U.S. Citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Non‑U.S. citizens interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States must apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in their home country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program for programs and application procedures available to applicants based outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study/Research Award — proposal and country specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright Study/Research Award is the traditional award opportunity where a candidate designs a proposal for a specific country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the Country Summaries for country‑specific program information, institutional contacts, and available opportunities when designing their proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: English Teaching Assistant (ETA) Award — role and objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Fulbright English Teaching Assistant programs place grantees in schools overseas to supplement local English language instruction and to provide a native speaker presence in the classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the list of countries offering ETA Awards to determine placement locations and program expectations for classroom responsibilities and community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fulbright‑Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health — eligibility & program specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Fulbright‑Fogarty Fellowships promote research training in public health and clinical research in resource‑limited settings. To participate, the applicant must be a U.S. citizen and meet specified academic status by the program start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By start of the program year, fellows must be an MD (and other professional degree) student who has completed their 3rd year, or a Ph.D. candidate who has completed their master’s‑level requirements (i.e., post‑qualifying exam). Other basic requirements and the application process are the same as any Fulbright U.S. Student Study/Research Grant. The Fogarty International Center (NIH) may provide support to the research training site, orientation for fellows, and a pre‑departure orientation in Washington, DC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fulbright‑National Geographic Award Program — thematic alignment & additional expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright‑National Geographic Award Program seeks proposals that undertake an in‑depth examination of globally relevant issues as an add‑on to the Fulbright Open Study/Research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded projects must incorporate science, storytelling, and/or education and must align with one or more of National Geographic Society’s six focus areas: Ocean, Land, Wildlife, Human Histories and Cultures, Space, or Planetary Health. Successful applicants receive standard Fulbright U.S. Student Study/Research benefits plus additional grant funds, access to National Geographic resources (trainings, events, mentorship), and other opportunities. The National Geographic Society expects to select up to five applicants for this award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application pathway requirement — apply through institution when enrolled
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are currently enrolled in a U.S. undergraduate or graduate program, you will apply through that institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if you are not currently resident at the institution, the campus Fulbright Program Adviser is the point of contact for application submission and campus‑level processes.
